questions.def: 'Whether' introduces a noun clause expressing doubt or choice.
questions.question: ___ he decides to go is his own business.

questions.def: 'Whether' is used to express doubt about a noun clause.
questions.question: I'm not sure ___ the meeting has been postponed.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ is what matters most.

questions.def: 'That' introduces a noun clause functioning as a complement.
questions.question: The problem is ___ we don't have enough resources.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause referring to a thing or event.
questions.question: Tell me ___ happened at the conference.

questions.def: 'What to + verb' introduces a noun clause acting as object.
questions.question: I'm still unsure ___.

questions.def: 'What' is used when the noun clause refers to the content.
questions.question: I was surprised by ___ she said.

questions.def: 'What' is used as the subject complement when unsure.
questions.question: It's unclear ___ they plan to do next.

questions.def: 'That' is correct here, introducing the noun clause.
questions.question: That he arrived late was surprising.

questions.def: 'Explain what' is grammatically correct in this instance.
questions.question: Can you ___ the problem is?

questions.def: 'What' refers to the content of the statement.
questions.question: ___ he said was a complete lie.

questions.def: 'Whether' introduces an alternative or doubt.
questions.question: The question is ___ we can afford it.

questions.def: The sentence needs 'what' to introduce the object noun clause.
questions.question: They ___ important information.

questions.def: 'That' introduces a fact or known information.
questions.question: It's obvious ___ she is very talented.

questions.def: 'Whether' implies a choice or uncertainty.
questions.question: I don't know ___ I should apply for the job.

questions.def: 'What they reported' functions as the subject of the sentence.
questions.question: ___ is concerning.

questions.def: 'How' introduces a noun clause explaining a manner.
questions.question: The key is ___ you manage your time.

questions.def: 'Whether' introduces doubt about a future event.
questions.question: I am unsure ___ he will arrive on time.

questions.def: 'Wonder what' introduces the noun clause correctly.
questions.question: I ___ will happen next.

questions.def: 'Whatever' introduces a noun clause meaning 'anything'.
questions.question: ___ you choose to do is up to you.

questions.def: 'What the weather is like' acts as a noun clause.
questions.question: It depends on ___ the weather is like.

questions.def: 'Suggested what' introduces a noun clause as the object.
questions.question: They ___ was a good idea.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ I need is a vacation.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause showing content.
questions.question: We discussed ___ we should do next.

questions.def: 'Whether' introduces a noun clause expressing doubt or a choice.
questions.question: ___ he will attend the meeting is still uncertain.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause acting as the subject; 'that' is incorrect.
questions.question: I'm not sure ___ caused the error in the system.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause acting as the subject of the sentence.
questions.question: ___ was said in the document remains confidential.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause indicating the content confirmed.
questions.question: The report confirms ___ we suspected all along.

questions.def: 'What' functions as the object of 'know' and subject of 'plans'.
questions.question: I don't know ___ he plans to do after graduation.

questions.def: The noun clause 'why he was late' is the object of 'explain'.
questions.question: He didn't ___ why he was late.
